TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures reliable data transmission through error checking, flow control, and retransmission of lost packets. It is suitable for applications where data integrity is crucial, such as web browsing, email, and file transfers. UDP (User Datagram Protocol), on the other hand, is a connectionless protocol that does not guarantee delivery or order of packets. It is faster and more efficient for real-time applications like video streaming, online gaming, and voice over IP (VoIP), where some data loss is acceptable.
